questions.question: What guarantees that another driver sees you?

options.text: Eye contact
Using a turn signal
Following another vehicle
Nothing

questions.correctAnswerText: Nothing
questions.explanation: Nothing guarantees that another driver sees you. Assume that any vehicle that can enter your path will. Stay alert and defensive.

questions.question: A car is entering the highway on a ramp to your right and may not see your motorcycle. What should you do?

options.text: Sound your horn.
Flash your lights.
Move to the left portion of your lane so they can share the lane, if necessary.
Move into another lane, if necessary.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move into another lane, if necessary.
questions.explanation: Give space to vehicles merging from an entrance ramp. Change lanes away from the ramp if possible. If you cannot change lanes, slow down to give them room to safely enter the highway.

questions.question: Your motorcycle is wobbling. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to stop the wobble.
Use the brakes gradually.
Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly release the throttle.
Downshift.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly release the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up, as this makes wobbling worse. Instead, grip the handlebars firmly without fighting the wobble. Slowly close the throttle to slow down. Move your weight forward and down. Pull off the road as soon as safely possible.

questions.question: Your front wheel locks up. What should you do?

options.text: Keep holding the brake until the skid stops.
Release the front brake and stop using it.
Release the front brake, then squeeze it quickly.
Release the front brake right away and apply it smoothly again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away and apply it smoothly again.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks, release the brake completely right away. Then apply the brake smoothly.

questions.question: When riding at night, what should you do?

options.text: Adjust your lane position as needed for changing conditions.
Travel faster than usual to reach your destination quicker.
Always use your low beam to see better.
Ride closer to the vehicle ahead of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Adjust your lane position as needed for changing conditions.
questions.explanation: Be flexible about where you position your motorcycle in your lane, especially at night. Use extra caution and safe riding practices when conditions are less than ideal.

questions.question: How should you sit on a motorcycle for proper control?

options.text: Sit so your arms steer the motorcycle, not hold you up.
Sit far back so your arms stay straight.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Drag your feet on the ground.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit so your arms steer the motorcycle, not hold you up.
questions.explanation: Sit so your arms control the motorcycle instead of supporting your body. Your arms should have a slight bend at the elbows. Keep your knees against the gas tank and your feet on the footrests to help with balance.

questions.question: How can you stop other drivers from sharing your lane?

options.text: Give other drivers dirty looks.
Ride in the center of your lane.
Ride on the left side of your lane.
Ride in a zigzag pattern.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: Riding in the center of your lane leaves little space on either side. This makes it harder for other drivers to try to share the lane with you.

questions.question: What is an advantage of wearing a leather jacket when riding?

options.text: It makes you look cool.
It is usually too warm to wear.
It protects you in a crash.
It should not be worn when riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: It protects you in a crash.
questions.explanation: Wear a long-sleeved jacket, preferably leather, when riding. Leather jackets protect your skin in a crash. In warm weather, many motorcycle jackets are designed to help keep you cool.

questions.question: When rain starts, what should you do?

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Pull over until the rain stops.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
Speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: Do not ride in the center of the lane when wet. Instead, ride in the tire tracks left by cars ahead of you. The left track is often best, but this depends on traffic and conditions.

questions.question: When slowing or stopping, when should you use both brakes?

options.text: Only when the pavement is wet.
Not very often.
Only in the city.
Every time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every time.
questions.explanation: Using both the front and rear brakes gives you the most stopping power. Use both brakes every time you slow down or stop.

questions.question: How do you lean a motorcycle for a turn?

options.text: Press the handgrip toward the direction of the turn.
Press the handgrip away from the direction of the turn.
Apply the front brake.
Apply the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip toward the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles lean to turn. Press the handgrip in the direction you want to go.

questions.question: Which item is NOT protective riding gear?

options.text: A leather jacket
Boots that cover the ankles
Hearing protection
Pants made of soft material

questions.correctAnswerText: Pants made of soft material
questions.explanation: Good protective gear includes a leather or sturdy jacket, pants made of leather or tough material, boots that cover your ankles, and hearing protection.

questions.question: What helps prevent crashes?

options.text: Skip using turn signals when changing lanes.
Follow other vehicles closely.
Watch only five feet ahead while riding.
Always be ready to avoid hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to avoid hazards.
questions.explanation: To avoid crashes, be visible to others. Use your signals, brake light, and good lane position. Keep space around your motorcycle. Watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you. Always be ready to avoid unexpected hazards.

questions.question: Where is the front brake lever on a motorcycle?

options.text: On the left handgrip
On the right handgrip
By the left foot peg
By the right foot peg

questions.correctAnswerText: On the right handgrip
questions.explanation: The front brake lever is on the right handgrip. Learn the location of all your motorcycle's controls before you ride.

questions.question: What is NOT helped by using a proper lane position?

options.text: Avoid other drivers' blind spots.
See and be seen better.
Go faster.
Set up for turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go faster.
questions.explanation: Proper lane position helps you see and be seen, avoid blind spots, and prepare for turns. It does not help you go faster.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, what should you do?

options.text: Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Choose to either brake or swerve.
Only use the front brake and do not swerve.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake.
questions.explanation: Do these actions separately, not at the same time. Braking while swerving can cause your motorcycle to fall over.

questions.question: What should you do at a blind intersection with a stop sign?

options.text: Stop at the sign then drive through.
Ignore the sign and move forward to look.
Stop at the sign, move forward slowly, stop again, and look for cross traffic.
Drive through without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at the sign, move forward slowly, stop again, and look for cross traffic.
questions.explanation: Stop at the stop sign. Then move forward and stop again near the crossroad. Lean forward and look around buildings, cars, or bushes to check for traffic. Keep your front wheel out of the crossroad.

questions.question: How can you reduce your reaction time?

options.text: Shift into neutral when slowing down.
Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
Pull the clutch in when turning.
Ride slower than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: In risky areas like intersections, shopping areas, school zones, and construction zones, keep your hands ready on the clutch and brakes. This reduces the time you need to react to hazards.

questions.question: What happens if your front tire goes flat while riding?

options.text: The steering will feel heavy.
The steering will feel loose.
The steering will feel the same.
The ride will feel too smooth.

questions.correctAnswerText: The steering will feel heavy.
questions.explanation: A flat front tire makes steering feel heavy. If your steering feels heavy, pull over and check your tires right away.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?

options.text: Never
Only during the day
Only at night
Day and night

questions.correctAnswerText: Day and night
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight. Wear bright colors and reflective materials at all times to stay visible.

questions.question: More than half of all motorcycle crashes involve riders with what experience level?

options.text: Less than six months of experience on their motorcycle.
Faulty ignition systems.
Distractions from passengers.
Riding at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Less than six months of experience on their motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Be extra careful when riding a motorcycle you are new to. Most motorcycle crashes happen to riders with less than six months of experience on their bike.

questions.question: How should you stop your motorcycle quickly?

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use only the rear brake.
Use the front brake first, then the rear brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: When you need to stop quickly, apply both brakes at the same time.

questions.question: What should a passenger do while you are riding?

options.text: Lean the same way you lean.
Hold onto the seat.
Sit as far back on the seat as possible.
Never hold onto you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean the same way you lean.
questions.explanation: Passengers should lean when you lean. They should sit forward without crowding you and hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding, what should you do?

options.text: Use both brakes and stop quickly.
Shift your weight toward the good tire.
Brake using only the good tire and steer toward the road edge.
Relax your grip on the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake using only the good tire and steer toward the road edge.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, grip the handlebars firmly, ease off the throttle, and go straight. Brake slowly using only the tire that is not flat. As you slow down, move to the side of the road, squeeze the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop your motorcycle quickly?

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use the front brake first.
Release the throttle and use the front brake.
Use both brakes at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply both the front and rear brakes at the same time.

questions.question: When should a motorcyclist shift gears?

options.text: While turning.
Before turning.
By changing power suddenly during a turn.
While braking throughout the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before turning.
questions.explanation: Change gears before you enter a turn.

questions.question: How do you maintain control of your motorcycle while turning?

options.text: Speed up before entering the turn.
Keep the motorcycle upright without leaning.
Look ahead through the turn to plan your path.
Stop completely before entering the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead through the turn to plan your path.
questions.explanation: To stay in control through a turn, look ahead by turning your head only. Slow down before the turn and lean your motorcycle in the right direction.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers about upcoming road hazards or conditions.

questions.question: When riding downhill on a motorcycle with a sidecar, how does stopping compare to riding without a sidecar?

options.text: Stopping is easier with a sidecar.
Stopping takes longer with a sidecar.
You cannot stop with a sidecar.
Stopping is about the same with or without a sidecar.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stopping takes longer with a sidecar.
questions.explanation: A sidecar adds weight to your motorcycle, which requires more braking power. Downhill riding also increases stopping distance. Together, these factors mean stopping takes longer when riding with a sidecar.

questions.question: How do headache, cold, and hay fever medications usually affect your body?

options.text: They make you sleepy.
They make you more alert.
They make you hungry.
They make it hard to concentrate.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make you sleepy.
questions.explanation: Most medications for headaches, colds, hay fever, allergies, and stress can make you sleepy and reduce your ability to ride safely. Always check how a medication affects you before riding.
